questions.stem: The average salary of \(25\) employees in a company is Rs. \(18000\). If the salary of each employee is increased by \(12\)%, what will be the new average salary?
questions.keySolution:
Original average salary = Rs. \(18000\)
Increase = \(12\)%
New average = \(18000 + 12\)% of \(18000\)
New average = \(18000 + \frac{12}{100} \times 18000\)
New average = \(18000 + 2160 = Rs. 20160\)

questions.stem: The average marks of \(30\) students is \(75\). If \(20\)% of students scored above \(90\) marks and their average is \(95\), what is the average of the remaining students?
questions.keySolution:
Total students = \(30\)
Students scoring above \(90\) = \(20\)% of \(30 = 6\) students
Remaining students = \(30 - 6 = 24\) students
Total marks of all students = \(30 \times 75 = 2250\)
Total marks of \(6\) students = \(6 \times 95 = 570\)
Total marks of remaining \(24\) students = \(2250 - 570 = 1680\)
Average of remaining students = \(\frac{1680}{24} = 70\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(5\) numbers is \(40\) and each number is increased by \(25\)%, what is the percentage increase in their average?
questions.keySolution:
Original average = \(40\)
When each number is increased by \(25\)%, the average also increases by \(25\)%
New average = \(40 + 25\)% of \(40 = 40 + 10 = 50\)
Percentage increase in average = \(\frac{50-40}{40} \times 100 = 25\)%

questions.stem: The average weight of \(12\) persons is \(60\) kg. If \(4\) persons leave the group and their average weight was \(25\)% more than the group average, what is the new average weight of the remaining persons?
questions.keySolution:
Total weight of \(12\) persons = \(12 \times 60 = 720\) kg
Average weight of \(4\) persons who left = \(60 + 25\)% of \(60 = 60 + 15 = 75\) kg
Total weight of \(4\) persons = \(4 \times 75 = 300\) kg
Remaining weight = \(720 - 300 = 420\) kg
Remaining persons = \(12 - 4 = 8\)
New average = \(\frac{420}{8} = 52.5\) kg

questions.stem: In a class, \(40\)% students are boys and \(60\)% are girls. If the average marks of boys is \(72\) and that of girls is \(78\), what is the overall average marks of the class?
questions.keySolution:
Let total students = \(100\)
Boys = \(40\)% of \(100 = 40\)
Girls = \(60\)% of \(100 = 60\)
Total marks of boys = \(40 \times 72 = 2880\)
Total marks of girls = \(60 \times 78 = 4680\)
Total marks = \(2880 + 4680 = 7560\)
Overall average = \(\frac{7560}{100} = 75.6\)

questions.stem: The average age of \(20\) members of a club is \(35\) years. If \(5\) new members join with an average age that is \(20\)% less than the current average, what will be the new average age?
questions.keySolution:
Total age of \(20\) members = \(20 \times 35 = 700\) years
Average age of \(5\) new members = \(35 - 20\)% of \(35 = 35 - 7 = 28\) years
Total age of \(5\) new members = \(5 \times 28 = 140\) years
Total age of all \(25\) members = \(700 + 140 = 840\) years
New average age = \(\frac{840}{25} = 33.6\) years

questions.stem: If \(30\)% of a number is added to its average with another number, the result is \(91\). If the other number is \(70\), find the first number.
questions.keySolution:
Let the first number = \(x\)
Average of \(x\) and \(70\) = \(\frac{x + 70}{2}\)
According to the question:
\(30\)% of \(x\) + Average = \(91\)
\(0.3x + \frac{x + 70}{2} = 91\)
\(0.3x + \frac{x}{2} + 35 = 91\)
\(0.3x + 0.5x = 56\)
\(0.8x = 56\)
\(x = 70\)

questions.stem: The average score of \(40\) students in an exam is \(65\). If \(15\)% of students failed and their average score was \(35\), what is the average score of students who passed?
questions.keySolution:
Total students = \(40\)
Failed students = \(15\)% of \(40 = 6\) students
Passed students = \(40 - 6 = 34\) students
Total score of all students = \(40 \times 65 = 2600\)
Total score of failed students = \(6 \times 35 = 210\)
Total score of passed students = \(2600 - 210 = 2390\)
Average score of passed students = \(\frac{2390}{34} = 70.29\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(10\) numbers decreases by \(8\)% when the largest number is replaced by \(24\), and the original average was \(50\), find the largest number.
questions.keySolution:
Original average = \(50\)
New average = \(50 - 8\)% of \(50 = 50 - 4 = 46\)
Sum of original \(10\) numbers = \(10 \times 50 = 500\)
Sum after replacement = \(10 \times 46 = 460\)
Decrease in sum = \(500 - 460 = 40\)
Largest number - \(24 = 40\)
Largest number = \(24 + 40 = 64\)

questions.stem: In a company, \(25\)% employees earn more than Rs. \(25000\) per month and their average salary is Rs. \(32000\). If the overall average salary is Rs. \(22000\), what is the average salary of the remaining employees?
questions.keySolution:
Let total employees = \(100\)
Employees earning > Rs. \(25000\) = \(25\)% of \(100 = 25\)
Remaining employees = \(100 - 25 = 75\)
Total salary of all employees = \(100 \times 22000 = 2200000\)
Total salary of \(25\) employees = \(25 \times 32000 = 800000\)
Total salary of remaining \(75\) employees = \(2200000 - 800000 = 1400000\)
Average salary of remaining employees = \(\frac{1400000}{75} = 18666.67\)

questions.stem: The average height of \(8\) students is \(160\) cm. If \(2\) students with heights \(25\)% above average join the group, what will be the new average height?
questions.keySolution:
Total height of \(8\) students = \(8 \times 160 = 1280\) cm
Height of each new student = \(160 + 25\)% of \(160 = 160 + 40 = 200\) cm
Total height of \(2\) new students = \(2 \times 200 = 400\) cm
Total height of all \(10\) students = \(1280 + 400 = 1680\) cm
New average height = \(\frac{1680}{10} = 168\) cm

questions.stem: If \(60\)% of students in a class have an average mark of \(80\) and the remaining \(40\)% have an average mark of \(70\), by what percentage is the overall average more than \(70\)?
questions.keySolution:
Let total students = \(100\)
Students with \(80\) marks = \(60\)
Students with \(70\) marks = \(40\)
Total marks = \(60 \times 80 + 40 \times 70 = 4800 + 2800 = 7600\)
Overall average = \(\frac{7600}{100} = 76\)
Percentage more than \(70\) = \(\frac{76-70}{70} \times 100 = \frac{6}{70} \times 100 = 8.57\)%

questions.stem: The average income of \(5\) families is Rs. \(45000\). If one family's income increases by \(40\)%, what is the percentage increase in the average income?
questions.keySolution:
Total income of \(5\) families = \(5 \times 45000 = 225000\)
Increase in one family's income = \(40\)% of \(45000 = 18000\)
New total income = \(225000 + 18000 = 243000\)
New average = \(\frac{243000}{5} = 48600\)
Percentage increase = \(\frac{48600-45000}{45000} \times 100 = \frac{3600}{45000} \times 100 = 8\)%

questions.stem: In a test, \(30\)% students scored above \(85\) marks with an average of \(92\). If \(45\)% students scored between \(60-85\) with an average of \(72\), what is the average of the remaining students if the overall average is \(74\)?
questions.keySolution:
Let total students = \(100\)
Students scoring above \(85\) = \(30\)
Students scoring \(60-85\) = \(45\)
Remaining students = \(100 - 30 - 45 = 25\)
Total marks of all students = \(100 \times 74 = 7400\)
Marks of students above \(85\) = \(30 \times 92 = 2760\)
Marks of students \(60-85\) = \(45 \times 72 = 3240\)
Marks of remaining students = \(7400 - 2760 - 3240 = 1400\)
Average of remaining students = \(\frac{1400}{25} = 56\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(12\) consecutive numbers is \(15.5\) and each number is increased by \(15\)%, what is the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Original average = \(15.5\)
When each number is increased by \(15\)%, the average also increases by \(15\)%
New average = \(15.5 + 15\)% of \(15.5\)
New average = \(15.5 + \frac{15}{100} \times 15.5\)
New average = \(15.5 + 2.325 = 17.825\)

questions.stem: The average price of \(15\) items is Rs. \(125\). If \(5\) items are sold at \(20\)% profit and \(10\) items at \(10\)% loss, what is the overall profit/loss percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Total cost = \(15 \times 125 = 1875\)
Selling price of \(5\) items = \(5 \times 125 \times 1.2 = 750\)
Selling price of \(10\) items = \(10 \times 125 \times 0.9 = 1125\)
Total selling price = \(750 + 1125 = 1875\)
Total cost price = \(1875\)
Profit/Loss = \(1875 - 1875 = 0\)
Therefore, \(0\)% (No profit/loss)

questions.stem: In a school, \(55\)% are boys and \(45\)% are girls. If the average weight of boys is \(15\)% more than girls and the overall average weight is \(48\) kg, find the average weight of girls.
questions.keySolution:
Let average weight of girls = \(x\) kg
Average weight of boys = \(x + 15\)% of \(x = 1.15x\) kg
Overall average = \(\frac{55 \times 1.15x + 45 \times x}{100}\)
\(48 = \frac{63.25x + 45x}{100}\)
\(48 = \frac{108.25x}{100}\)
\(4800 = 108.25x\)
\(x = \frac{4800}{108.25} = 44.33\) kg

questions.stem: The average marks of \(20\) students decrease by \(5\)% when a new student joins. If the new student scored \(40\) marks, what was the original average?
questions.keySolution:
Let original average = \(x\)
New average = \(x - 5\)% of \(x = 0.95x\)
Sum of marks of \(20\) students = \(20x\)
Sum of marks of \(21\) students = \(20x + 40\)
New average = \(\frac{20x + 40}{21} = 0.95x\)
\(20x + 40 = 21 \times 0.95x\)
\(20x + 40 = 19.95x\)
\(0.05x = 40\)
\(x = 800\)

questions.stem: If \(25\)% of a class has an average age of \(22\) years and the remaining \(75\)% has an average age of \(18\) years, what is the average age of the whole class?
questions.keySolution:
Let total students = \(100\)
Students with age \(22\) years = \(25\)
Students with age \(18\) years = \(75\)
Total age = \(25 \times 22 + 75 \times 18 = 550 + 1350 = 1900\) years
Average age = \(\frac{1900}{100} = 19\) years

questions.stem: The average salary of \(16\) employees increases by \(12.5\)% when the boss joins them. If the boss's salary is Rs. \(75000\), what was the average salary of the employees?
questions.keySolution:
Let original average salary = \(x\)
New average = \(x + 12.5\)% of \(x = 1.125x\)
Sum of salaries of \(16\) employees = \(16x\)
Sum of salaries of \(17\) people = \(16x + 75000\)
New average = \(\frac{16x + 75000}{17} = 1.125x\)
\(16x + 75000 = 17 \times 1.125x\)
\(16x + 75000 = 19.125x\)
\(75000 = 3.125x\)
\(x = 24000\)

questions.stem: In a factory, \(40\)% workers are skilled with average wage Rs. \(350\) per day and \(60\)% are unskilled with average wage \(20\)% less than skilled workers. What is the average daily wage of all workers?
questions.keySolution:
Skilled workers = \(40\)%
Unskilled workers = \(60\)%
Wage of skilled workers = Rs. \(350\)
Wage of unskilled workers = \(350 - 20\)% of \(350 = 350 - 70 = Rs. 280\)
Average wage = \(\frac{40 \times 350 + 60 \times 280}{100}\)
Average wage = \(\frac{14000 + 16800}{100} = \frac{30800}{100} = Rs. 308\)

questions.stem: The average score of a cricket team in \(10\) matches is \(245\). If in the next \(5\) matches their average score increases by \(8\)%, what will be their overall average after \(15\) matches?
questions.keySolution:
Total score in first \(10\) matches = \(10 \times 245 = 2450\)
Average score in next \(5\) matches = \(245 + 8\)% of \(245 = 245 + 19.6 = 264.6\)
Total score in next \(5\) matches = \(5 \times 264.6 = 1323\)
Total score in \(15\) matches = \(2450 + 1323 = 3773\)
Overall average = \(\frac{3773}{15} = 251.53\)

questions.stem: If \(35\)% of students in a college are from Science stream with average marks \(78\), \(40\)% from Commerce with average marks \(15\)% less than Science, and remaining from Arts with average marks \(70\), find the overall average.
questions.keySolution:
Science students = \(35\)%, Average = \(78\)
Commerce students = \(40\)%, Average = \(78 - 15\)% of \(78 = 78 - 11.7 = 66.3\)
Arts students = \(100 - 35 - 40 = 25\)%, Average = \(70\)
Overall average = \(\frac{35 \times 78 + 40 \times 66.3 + 25 \times 70}{100}\)
Overall average = \(\frac{2730 + 2652 + 1750}{100} = \frac{7132}{100} = 71.32\)

questions.stem: The average production of a factory for \(6\) months is \(4500\) units. If production increases by \(18\)% in the \(7\)th month, what will be the average production for \(7\) months?
questions.keySolution:
Total production for \(6\) months = \(6 \times 4500 = 27000\) units
Production in \(7\)th month = \(4500 + 18\)% of \(4500 = 4500 + 810 = 5310\) units
Total production for \(7\) months = \(27000 + 5310 = 32310\) units
Average production for \(7\) months = \(\frac{32310}{7} = 4615.71\) units

questions.stem: In an examination, \(20\)% students got A grade with average marks \(92\), \(50\)% got B grade with average marks \(78\), and remaining got C grade. If the overall average is \(75\), what is the average marks of C grade students?
questions.keySolution:
A grade students = \(20\)%, B grade = \(50\)%, C grade = \(30\)%
Let average marks of C grade = \(x\)
Overall average = \(\frac{20 \times 92 + 50 \times 78 + 30 \times x}{100} = 75\)
\(1840 + 3900 + 30x = 7500\)
\(30x = 7500 - 5740 = 1760\)
\(x = \frac{1760}{30} = 58.67\)

questions.stem: If the average of \(n\) numbers is \(A\) and each number is increased by \(k\)%, what is the percentage change in the average?
questions.keySolution:
When each number is increased by \(k\)%, the average also increases by the same percentage \(k\)%
This is because: If all numbers are \(x_1, x_2, ..., x_n\)
New numbers become \((1 + \frac{k}{100})x_1, (1 + \frac{k}{100})x_2, ..., (1 + \frac{k}{100})x_n\)
New average = \((1 + \frac{k}{100}) \times \frac{x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_n}{n} = (1 + \frac{k}{100}) \times A\)
Percentage change = \(k\)%

questions.stem: The average monthly expense of a family decreases by \(6\)% when they stop eating outside. If they were spending Rs. \(2400\) per month on outside food, what was their original average monthly expense?
questions.keySolution:
Let original average monthly expense = \(x\)
Decrease = \(6\)% of \(x = 0.06x\)
This decrease equals outside food expense = Rs. \(2400\)
\(0.06x = 2400\)
\(x = \frac{2400}{0.06} = 40000\)
Original average monthly expense = Rs. \(40000\)

questions.stem: If \(80\)% of students passed an exam with average marks \(72\) and \(20\)% failed with average marks \(35\), what is the overall class average?
questions.keySolution:
Passed students = \(80\)%, Average marks = \(72\)
Failed students = \(20\)%, Average marks = \(35\)
Overall average = \(\frac{80 \times 72 + 20 \times 35}{100}\)
Overall average = \(\frac{5760 + 700}{100} = \frac{6460}{100} = 64.6\)

questions.stem: The average age of a group of \(20\) people decreases by \(10\)% when \(5\) people aged \(60\) years each leave and \(5\) people aged \(30\) years each join. What was the original average age?
questions.keySolution:
Let original average age = \(x\) years
New average age = \(x - 10\)% of \(x = 0.9x\) years
Original total age = \(20x\)
Age decrease = \(5 \times 60 - 5 \times 30 = 300 - 150 = 150\) years
New total age = \(20x - 150\)
New average = \(\frac{20x - 150}{20} = 0.9x\)
\(20x - 150 = 18x\)
\(2x = 150\)
\(x = 75\) years

questions.stem: In a school, \(45\)% students are in primary section with average fee Rs. \(8000\), \(35\)% in secondary with average fee \(25\)% more than primary, and \(20\)% in senior secondary. If overall average fee is Rs. \(9500\), find the average fee of senior secondary students.
The average marks of \(18\) students is \(68\). If \(2\) students leave whose marks were \(30\)% below average, what will be the new average?
questions.keySolution:
Original total marks = \(18 \times 68 = 1224\)
Marks of each leaving student = \(68 - 30\)% of \(68 = 68 - 20.4 = 47.6\)
Total marks of \(2\) leaving students = \(2 \times 47.6 = 95.2\)
Remaining total marks = \(1224 - 95.2 = 1128.8\)
New average = \(\frac{1128.8}{16} = 70.55\)

questions.stem: If the average income of \(10\) people is Rs. \(25000\) and the income of the richest person is \(60\)% more than the average, what is the average income of the remaining \(9\) people?
questions.keySolution:
Total income of \(10\) people = \(10 \times 25000 = 250000\)
Income of richest person = \(25000 + 60\)% of \(25000 = 25000 + 15000 = 40000\)
Total income of remaining \(9\) people = \(250000 - 40000 = 210000\)
Average income of remaining \(9\) people = \(\frac{210000}{9} = 23333.33\)

questions.stem: In a test, \(35\)% students scored above \(80\) marks, \(40\)% scored between \(60-80\) marks, and \(25\)% scored below \(60\) marks. If the average marks of the middle group is \(15\)% more than the lowest group and \(20\)% less than the highest group, find the overall average if the highest group average is \(88\).
questions.keySolution:
Highest group average = \(88\)
Middle group average = \(88 - 20\)% of \(88 = 88 - 17.6 = 70.4\)
Lowest group average = \(\frac{70.4}{1.15} = 61.22\)
Overall average = \(\frac{35 \times 88 + 40 \times 70.4 + 25 \times 61.22}{100}\)
Overall average = \(\frac{3080 + 2816 + 1530.5}{100} = \frac{7426.5}{100} = 74.27\)

questions.stem: The average expenditure of a family of \(5\) members is Rs. \(18000\) per month. If \(2\) members leave and their expenditure was \(40\)% more than the family average, what is the new average expenditure?
questions.keySolution:
Total expenditure of \(5\) members = \(5 \times 18000 = 90000\)
Expenditure of each leaving member = \(18000 + 40\)% of \(18000 = 18000 + 7200 = 25200\)
Total expenditure of \(2\) leaving members = \(2 \times 25200 = 50400\)
Remaining expenditure = \(90000 - 50400 = 39600\)
New average expenditure = \(\frac{39600}{3} = 13200\)

questions.stem: In a company, the average productivity of \(24\) employees is \(85\) units per day. If the productivity of each employee increases by \(18\)%, what will be the total increase in daily production?
questions.keySolution:
Original total production = \(24 \times 85 = 2040\) units
Increase in production = \(18\)% of \(2040 = \frac{18}{100} \times 2040 = 367.2\) units
Alternatively:
Increase per employee = \(18\)% of \(85 = 15.3\) units
Total increase = \(24 \times 15.3 = 367.2\) units

questions.stem: The average score of \(8\) batsmen in a cricket match is \(42\). If \(3\) batsmen who scored \(25\)% above average are replaced by \(3\) new batsmen who score \(15\)% below average, what is the new average score?
questions.keySolution:
Original total score = \(8 \times 42 = 336\)
Score of each leaving batsman = \(42 + 25\)% of \(42 = 42 + 10.5 = 52.5\)
Score of each new batsman = \(42 - 15\)% of \(42 = 42 - 6.3 = 35.7\)
Change in total score = \(3 \times (35.7 - 52.5) = 3 \times (-16.8) = -50.4\)
New total score = \(336 - 50.4 = 285.6\)
New average = \(\frac{285.6}{8} = 35.7\)

questions.stem: If \(70\)% of items in a store cost less than Rs. \(500\) with average price Rs. \(320\), and \(30\)% cost more than Rs. \(500\) with average price Rs. \(850\), what is the overall average price?
questions.keySolution:
Items costing < Rs. \(500\): \(70\)% with average Rs. \(320\)
Items costing > Rs. \(500\): \(30\)% with average Rs. \(850\)
Overall average = \(\frac{70 \times 320 + 30 \times 850}{100}\)
Overall average = \(\frac{22400 + 25500}{100} = \frac{47900}{100} = Rs. 479\)

questions.stem: The average temperature for \(7\) days was \(28°C\). If the temperature on the \(8\)th day is \(15\)% higher than the weekly average, what will be the new average temperature for \(8\) days?
questions.keySolution:
Total temperature for \(7\) days = \(7 \times 28 = 196°C\)
Temperature on \(8\)th day = \(28 + 15\)% of \(28 = 28 + 4.2 = 32.2°C\)
Total temperature for \(8\) days = \(196 + 32.2 = 228.2°C\)
New average temperature = \(\frac{228.2}{8} = 28.525°C\)

questions.stem: In a survey, \(45\)% respondents rated a product as excellent with average rating \(9.2\), \(35\)% as good with rating \(12\)% less than excellent, and \(20\)% as average with rating \(6.5\). Find the overall average rating.
questions.keySolution:
Excellent: \(45\)% with rating \(9.2\)
Good: \(35\)% with rating \(9.2 - 12\)% of \(9.2 = 9.2 - 1.104 = 8.096\)
Average: \(20\)% with rating \(6.5\)
Overall average = \(\frac{45 \times 9.2 + 35 \times 8.096 + 20 \times 6.5}{100}\)
Overall average = \(\frac{414 + 283.36 + 130}{100} = \frac{827.36}{100} = 8.27\)

questions.stem: The average monthly sales of a shop for \(9\) months is Rs. \(85000\). If sales in the \(10\)th month increase by \(25\)% over the monthly average, and in the \(11\)th month decrease by \(10\)% from the \(10\)th month, what is the average monthly sales for \(11\) months?
In a class of \(50\) students, \(60\)% are boys. If the average marks of boys is \(78\) and the overall average is \(75\), what is the average marks of girls?
questions.keySolution:
Total students = \(50\)
Boys = \(60\)% of \(50 = 30\)
Girls = \(50 - 30 = 20\)
Total marks of all students = \(50 \times 75 = 3750\)
Total marks of boys = \(30 \times 78 = 2340\)
Total marks of girls = \(3750 - 2340 = 1410\)
Average marks of girls = \(\frac{1410}{20} = 70.5\)

questions.stem: The average weight of \(12\) boxes is \(25\) kg. If \(4\) boxes are removed and their average weight was \(35\)% more than the group average, what percentage change occurs in the new average weight?
questions.keySolution:
Total weight of \(12\) boxes = \(12 \times 25 = 300\) kg
Weight of each removed box = \(25 + 35\)% of \(25 = 25 + 8.75 = 33.75\) kg
Total weight of \(4\) removed boxes = \(4 \times 33.75 = 135\) kg
Remaining weight = \(300 - 135 = 165\) kg
New average weight = \(\frac{165}{8} = 20.625\) kg
Percentage change = \(\frac{20.625 - 25}{25} \times 100 = \frac{-4.375}{25} \times 100 = -17.5\)%

questions.stem: In a manufacturing unit, \(40\)% machines produce \(200\) units each daily, \(35\)% produce \(15\)% more than the first group, and \(25\)% produce \(10\)% less than the first group. What is the average daily production per machine?
questions.keySolution:
First group: \(40\)% with \(200\) units each
Second group: \(35\)% with \(200 + 15\)% of \(200 = 200 + 30 = 230\) units each
Third group: \(25\)% with \(200 - 10\)% of \(200 = 200 - 20 = 180\) units each
Average production = \(\frac{40 \times 200 + 35 \times 230 + 25 \times 180}{100}\)
Average production = \(\frac{8000 + 8050 + 4500}{100} = \frac{20550}{100} = 205.5\) units

questions.stem: The average price of \(20\) items increases from Rs. \(450\) to Rs. \(495\) when \(5\) items are replaced. If the average price of the \(5\) new items is Rs. \(720\), what was the average price of the \(5\) replaced items?
questions.keySolution:
Original total price = \(20 \times 450 = 9000\)
New total price = \(20 \times 495 = 9900\)
Increase in total price = \(9900 - 9000 = 900\)
Total price of \(5\) new items = \(5 \times 720 = 3600\)
Total price of \(5\) replaced items = \(3600 - 900 = 2700\)
Average price of \(5\) replaced items = \(\frac{2700}{5} = 540\)
